title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: No mathematical error on this page itself. The assertion that supports are closed under ≪° but not under ⊴ cannot be checked without the definitions of At 1-At 4 and of ≪°, which are not on this page.

ideas.what: Swapping the names 'magasin'/'atelier' and renaming axioms Mag1-4 to At1-4
A symmetric irreflexive relation |∘| on a set defines a family of 'supports' stable under arbitrary intersections, with complement an anti-involution (complete ortholattice)
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space; complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets (polarity/Galois connection)
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Birkhoff (Lattice Theory, 1940, polarities); Dacey 1968; Foulis-Randall (orthogonality spaces, quantum logic)

ideas.what: Supports required to be closed under a second relation ≪° but not under the order ⊴
ideas.modern_name: closure system compatible with an auxiliary relation; loosely akin to regular-open/way-below conditions

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently re-derived the orthogonality-space → complete-ortholattice construction (the basic structure of quantum logic) as part of his 'atelier'/'spatios' foundational project. No known link to the quantum-logic literature is made, and his combination of it with an order ⊴ and a relation ≪° appears nowhere in print.
missed.quote: La donnée de |∘|, relation symétrique antiréflexive, nous permet de définir un ensemble de parties particulières de 𝒜, appelées "supports"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's late foundational work on 'spaces' via orthocomplemented lattices. The mathematics itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is the standard ortholattice of an orthogonality relation. What is mildly notable is that it appears inside Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 'ateliers' framework, with an extra closure condition under ≪°, but nothing here is new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'relation symétrique non réflexive' likely reads 'relation symétrique antiréflexive' (the line break gives '.ntiréflexive').
The '37' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number; '40' at the bottom is the archive folio.
The struck phrase after 'je ne vais plus le noter M, il faut' is uncertain; possibly 'revoir la convenance de ses notations' (struck), followed by 'mais 𝒜, donc'.
